root.name: Three Knights Opening: Winawer Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Nc3 f5

overview: Black answers 3.Nc3 with the Schliemann-type 3...f5, hitting e4. White can take 4.exf5 or 4.Nxe5 and aims for central control and an extra pawn; Black aims for open lines, ...e4 or ...fxe4 and quick development. The game is double-edged and tactical.

white_ideas.idea: Take the pawn on f5 or e5 and consolidate
Play d2-d4 to open the centre
Develop Bc4/Bb5 against the exposed Black king

black_ideas.idea: Develop quickly and use the f-file and Qh4
Recover the pawn with active pieces

typical_structures.structure: Black f-pawn exchanged for e4 pawn, White knights centralised

character.notes: The move 3...f5 weakens Black's king and invites tactics.

gambit.notes: Black usually gives a pawn for open lines and development, as in the Schliemann.

soundness.notes: The Winawer/Gothic idea is treated as risky; White usually has a pleasant extra pawn.

structure.notes: Centre opens early with e-file and f-file pressure.

approach.notes: Rare; seldom chosen by strong players.

level.notes: Early tactics need to be known.

gambit.reason: Black is offering a pawn in most lines, similar to the Schliemann.

soundness.reason: Considered inferior; White gets a pawn up.

structure.reason: Early exchanges on f5/e4 open the centre.

plans.reason: Black plays for activity after offering a pawn.
